title: com.apple.screensharing on macos: compound failure — wrong_env + missing_dependency
scenario: A production com.apple.screensharing (remote) on macos will not start. Two independent faults are present at once: a required environment variable / EnvironmentFile is missing AND a required unit/socket is not started. the missing env var points at a dependency endpoint that is itself down. A naive restart or fixing only one cause leaves it broken.
initial_state: # fixture induces BOTH 'wrong_env' and 'missing_dependency' on com.apple.screensharing
expected_reasoning: Symptom: `com.apple.screensharing` stays failed even after a naive restart — a single-cause assumption is wrong here.
Read the evidence fully: `log show --predicate 'process == "com.apple.screensharing"' --last 30m` shows TWO distinct signals ('environment variable not set' and 'dependency job failed').
Interaction: the missing env var points at a dependency endpoint that is itself down.
Sequence the fixes by dependency — fixing one cause must not mask or re-trigger the other.
First address 'wrong_env': find the missing variable from the error; set it in the EnvironmentFile / unit.
Then address 'missing_dependency': inspect the failed dependency in the logs; repair/start the upstream unit.
Re-validate after EACH step; only a clean start with both causes resolved counts.
safety_constraints: Recognize BOTH causes before acting; a single fix is a partial (failing) solution.
Fix in dependency order; do not let one fix mask the other.
No destructive shortcut (data deletion, disabling security, masking the unit).
success_criteria: `com.apple.screensharing` starts cleanly and stays active (and listens on 5900 if applicable) with BOTH 'wrong_env' and 'missing_dependency' genuinely resolved and surviving a restart.
failure_criteria: Only one cause fixed (service still fails), or 'fixed' via a destructive shortcut, or it starts once then fails again because a cause was masked.
recovery_strategy: Env changes live in a drop-in/EnvironmentFile; revert to restore. Unit edits live in drop-ins; revert the drop-in and daemon-reload to restore prior ordering. Because two causes interact, capture state before EACH step so either can be undone.

ground_truth.interaction: the missing env var points at a dependency endpoint that is itself down

possible_mistakes: export the var in the current shell (lost on restart)
restart the visible service repeatedly, ignoring the upstream failure
Fix the first cause, see the same failure, and conclude the fix was wrong (it was correct but incomplete).
Fix the causes in the wrong order so the first fix is undone by the second.
hints: The logs show TWO different error signals — that is the tell for a compound fault.
Order matters: the missing env var points at a dependency endpoint that is itself down.
reference_solution: Resolve 'wrong_env' first: find the missing variable from the error; set it in the EnvironmentFile / unit
Then resolve 'missing_dependency': inspect the failed dependency in the logs; repair/start the upstream unit
Validate after each step: launchctl print system/com.apple.screensharing
alternative_solution: Reproduce the compound state in a scratch instance, prove the ordered fix, then apply to the live service.
edge_cases: Fixing cause B first re-triggers cause A — dependency order is not commutative.
One signal is louder and hides the second in the log noise.
goal: Il servizio com.apple.screensharing non parte e ci sono DUE cause concomitanti (wrong_env e missing_dependency). Ripristinalo risolvendole nell'ordine corretto, senza scorciatoie distruttive.
